A break-in that everyone “kind of saw coming” because the back row had no lights and no one checked it after 6 p.m. Good parking lot safety tips are not complicated. Tailgating security: what it is and how to prevent unauthorized access

Tailgating security sounds like something that should be easy to stop. Someone walks in behind an employee, the door closes, problem solved. Except that is exactly why it works. It is quick, awkward to challenge, and usually disguised as normal human behavior: holding a door, helping someone with packages, letting a vendor hurry in. For…

Workplace theft prevention usually starts with something small and annoying. A cash drawer is short again. A few tools disappear. Inventory counts are off, but nobody can explain why. Someone keeps using the wrong door after hours. None of it feels big enough to panic over, so it gets brushed off. Then it keeps happening….

Security Guard Incident Report: What to Include and How to Write One

A security guard incident report is easy to ignore until something goes sideways. Then everyone wants the details. Who was there? What time did it happen? Did the guard call anyone? Was there video?
